neighbours.label: words for a material's physical behaviour or property: expanding, sticking, stretching (expand, sticky, ductile)
fire: In hot weather the steel rails expand, so engineers leave small gaps between them.
Pine resin is sticky enough to trap small insects on the bark.
Gold is so ductile that a single gram can be drawn into a long wire.
As the dough rises, it expands to nearly twice its size in the bowl.
Wet clay feels sticky and clings to the potter's hands.
When the star swelled, its outer layers expanded past the inner planets.
Rubber bands become brittle in the cold and less elastic over time.
The foam insulation swells and fills every gap in the wall.
quiet: In hot weather the trains run less often, so engineers leave early.
Pine forests are home to many small insects living in the bark.
Gold is so expensive that a single gram can cost a week's wages.
As the dough rests, the baker cleans the counter and the bowl.
Wet clay is shaped on a wheel by the potter's hands.
When the star was discovered, astronomers named it after a poet.
Rubber bands are sold in bags of a hundred at the stationery shop.
The foam insulation was delivered on Tuesday and stored in the shed.

notes: Weak pole (max ~10) with no dominant token; top examples are sticky, expanded, ductile, expand, generate. Best guess at the shared pattern; low confidence.
